sections.content: How many people are "construction and building trades (other)"?

233,675 people

were counted on the census as "construction and building trades (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may undertake a variety of tasks in the construction, alteration, maintenance and repair of buildings, steeples, industrial chimneys and other tall structures, and of underwater structures not elsewhere classified.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "construction and building trades (other)" there were more men than women (97.8% compared with 2.2%).

This means "construction and building trades (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled construction and building trades".

Men made up 97.8% and women made up 2.2% of "construction and building trades (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "construction and building trades (other)" included:

  • electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers
  • welding trades
  • vehicle body builders and repairers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "construction and building trades (other)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "construction and building trades (other)", 14% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "construction and building trades (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "construction and building trades (other)" included:

  • window cleaners
  • cleaning and housekeeping managers and supervisors
  • other vocational and industrial trainers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "construction and building trades (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "construction and building trades (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "construction and building trades (other)", 7.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (79.5% compared with 20.5%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (73.6%) than an employee (26.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
